statement: A 3 by 3 by 3 cube is built from 27 small cubes. The cube in the middle of each face is pulled out, and so is the centre cube. How many small cubes remain?

choices.misconception: I counted the cubes that were pulled out instead of the cubes that are left.
I pulled out the six face middles but forgot the cube at the very centre.
I forgot the top and bottom faces, so I only pulled out four face middles and the centre cube.
I counted only the three faces I can see at once, so I pulled out three face middles and the centre cube.

hints: How many faces does a cube have?
Count how many small cubes are removed, then take that away from 27. Every face has one middle cube, and the centre cube is one more on top of those.
A cube has 6 faces, so 6 face middles come out, and then the centre cube makes 7 removed in all.

solutions.reliable: A cube has 6 faces, and each face has one middle cube, so 6 small cubes come out. The very centre cube is one more, so 7 are removed. That leaves 27 - 7 = 20. The transferable idea: count what is removed carefully, including the parts you cannot see, then subtract from the whole.
solutions.elegant: What is left is the 8 corner cubes and the 12 edge-middle cubes, because those are the only small cubes that are neither a face middle nor the centre: 8 + 12 = 20.

whyOnTest: Building with unit cubes rewards counting hidden faces and hidden cubes, which is exactly what the wrong totals forget.
author: Devansh Sanghavi
